concerns: Proposal text is truncated mid-sentence ('current_evidence' and 'proposed_change' end at 'compar'); the comparison methodology is therefore not fully specified

Per-candidate horizons create horizon-selection bias: if the window is chosen where profit materializes, that is label leakage. Each candidate's horizon must be fixed from its pre-registered stated design, never tuned post hoc on holdout performance
Replaying sealed holdouts consumes their sealing property; repeated replays inflate false discovery across the challenger pool. Cap replay count and log every run in ExperimentRegistry
A positive result must not loosen the validated-state gate directly; any gate redesign still requires fresh forward OOS validation through the standard promote.py gates
affected_files lists bot/intel/ and bot/ai_council/ (runtime surfaces) but the work is research-side; runtime gate logic should remain untouched until the research conclusion is accepted
Outcomes must be net of the runner's spread/slippage assumptions across the full extended executable window, matching AGENTS.md rule 6
votes.reason: Historical replay of sealed holdouts with per-candidate horizons is a cheap, read-only research experiment with clean rollback and no broker interaction; it directly tests a plausible gate-truncation hypothesis and the per-candidate-horizon economics it depends on were recently exposed in research reports. Safe to test provided horizon selection cannot peek at outcomes.
